test.why: S1: npm ci needs a lockfile; its config list says --ignore-scripts outranks allowing dependency install scripts. S2: it skips the project's own scripts too (prepare, postinstall), so such a project needs its own test command. Unverified: dependency scripts skipped on every npm version (seen once).

security.why: S4 only defines --audit-level (lowest severity giving a non-zero exit) and says audit sends a description of the dependencies to the registry. The level high is an UNVERIFIED design choice.

conventions.rule: Commit package-lock.json; it records the exact dependency tree so later installs rebuild the same one.
Install with npm ci in CI: it needs an existing lockfile, errors when the lockfile and package.json differ, removes node_modules first and never writes package.json or the lockfile.
Keep test setup in the package.json test script or in pretest/posttest: npm test runs pretest before it and posttest after it.
Do not rely on pretest or posttest when ignore-scripts is set: npm test then still runs the test script but skips them (the setting is false by default).
Set strict in tsconfig.json compilerOptions; it turns on the whole family of strict type checks.
Type-check without writing files using the noEmit option (tsc --noEmit).

With Node's built-in test runner (node --test), name test files *.test, *-test, *_test, test-* or test (.js/.cjs/.mjs, or .ts/.cts/.mts), or put them in a test directory; otherwise pass the file globs.
If the project uses ESLint, run eslint with no file arguments to lint the current directory; its exit code is 1 when errors are found and 2 for a configuration or internal problem.

dod.item: npm test runs the package.json test script and it passes
npm ci succeeds: package-lock.json is committed and matches package.json
npm audit --audit-level=high exits 0: no known vulnerability at high severity or above
If the project uses ESLint, eslint exits 0: no lint errors

S1.evidence: npm ci needs an existing lockfile, exits with an error instead of updating it when it disagrees with package.json, removes node_modules first and never writes package.json or lockfiles. Its config list says ignore-scripts outranks allowing dependency install scripts.

S2.evidence: The ignore-scripts setting (default false) stops npm running scripts from package.json files; npm test and npm run still run the script you name, but not its pre or post scripts. It does not say whether dependencies' install scripts are covered.

S3.evidence: npm test runs the command in the test property of the scripts object in package.json. The page does not describe exit codes.

S4.evidence: npm audit submits a description of the project's dependencies to the registry and needs a lockfile by default. With vulnerabilities found, the exit code depends on --audit-level, the minimum severity (info to critical) that gives a non-zero exit; none found gives 0.

S5.evidence: package-lock.json is meant to be committed to source repositories. It describes the exact dependency tree that was generated, so later installs reproduce the same dependencies.

S6.evidence: npm test goes through the stages pretest, test and posttest, and pre and post scripts with a matching name run around any script. The page says nothing about ignore-scripts.

S7.evidence: The strict compiler option enables a wide range of type checking behavior, and turning it on is equivalent to enabling all the options of the strict-mode family.

S8.evidence: node --test runs files matching default patterns: *.test, *-test, *_test, test-*, test and anything under a test directory, as .js/.cjs/.mjs, and also .ts/.cts/.mts unless --no-strip-types is given; or the globs passed. A failing test sets exit code 1. Stable since v20.

S9.evidence: With no file arguments ESLint lints the current directory. Exit code 0 means no lint errors, 1 means at least one error, 2 means a configuration problem or internal error.

S10.evidence: The --noEmit compiler flag disables emitting files from a compilation. The page does not say whether type errors are still reported or what exit code tsc returns.
